claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great. Now, do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money) at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep, you know, buying him clothes, helping with school things, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine your eligibility, I need to understand the amount you're contributing. 

Are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide (or the equivalent in kind through things like clothes, food, school items, etc.)? Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, or £16.95 per week for additional children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute more than that - it works out to about £26 a week when I add it all up.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One final question: Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - he's been in hospital for a while now. It's been a few months, really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear Alex has been in hospital. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to understand this situation better.

How many weeks has Alex been in hospital so far?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, this affects your eligibility. However, there is an exception to the rule.

Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital (for example, on items for him, travel to visit him, or other expenses for his benefit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I'm not entirely sure what counts as "regularly spending" - I mean, I help out when I can, but I don't know if that's what you mean by regular spending.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your uncertainty. Let me clarify: "regularly spending money" would mean you're consistently contributing financially towards Alex's needs while he's in hospital. This could include things like:

- Buying items for him (toys, books, clothes, toiletries)
- Paying for travel costs to visit him
- Purchasing things he needs or enjoys
- Any other expenses you're paying for his benefit

Are you making these kinds of financial contributions for Alex on a consistent basis while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know if what I'm doing counts as consistent enough. I help when I can, but I'm not sure if it meets the requirements you're describing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your uncertainty. Let me ask this more specifically: 

Over the past few weeks, approximately how often have you been spending money on Alex or for his benefit while he's been in hospital - would you say weekly, monthly, or less frequently than that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm really not sure - it's been difficult to keep track. Some weeks I manage to do more than others, but I couldn't say exactly how often it's been.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is difficult to quantify, especially during such a challenging time. Let me ask a different way to help clarify:

In a typical month while Alex has been in hospital, would you say you've spent any money at all on him or for his benefit (such as visiting him, buying him items, or anything else for him)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Look, I'm just not certain about the details. Some months have been better than others, and it's hard to say what's typical. I really can't give you a clear answer on that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is uncertain for you. Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

You've told me that:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you, but you contribute about £26 per week towards his upkeep (more than the Child Benefit amount)
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks (more than the 12-week threshold)
- You're uncertain about whether you're regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital

The key issue here is that once a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you would normally no longer be entitled to Child Benefit **unless** you regularly spend money on them. Since you're uncertain about whether your spending while he's been in hospital meets the "regularly spending" requirement, I cannot definitively determine your eligibility.

## Assessment Result

Based on our conversation, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**What works in your favor:**
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- You contribute about £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit threshold ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓

**The issue:**
Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks, which is more than the 12-week threshold. After 12 weeks in hospital, you would normally lose entitlement to Child Benefit **unless** you regularly spend money on him during his hospital stay.

Since you're uncertain about whether your spending on Alex while he's been in hospital meets the "regularly spending" requirement, I cannot determine whether you qualify for the exception.

**What you should do:**
I recommend you **contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly**. They can:
- Review your specific spending pattern on Alex
- Determine if it meets the "regularly spending" requirement
- Make a formal decision about your eligibility

You can contact them by phone or post - their contact details are available on the gov.uk website under "contact HMRC about Child Benefit."
